subject: Meet BLADE: The King of Graffiti
preheader: 5,000 trains, a Sotheby’s cover, and original work you can own.
bio_paragraph_1: BLADE, born in the Bronx as Steven Ogburn, began painting graffiti in 1972. Known for his whole-cars, he has painted more than 5,000 trains over the course of his career.
bio_paragraph_2: He earned his title as “the King of Graffiti,” exhibiting his first works on canvas in a European art show in 1981 and appearing on the cover of the Sotheby’s catalog in 2005 — the first living artist to do so since Andy Warhol.
bio_paragraph_3: His “Mainstreams” canvas, painted in spray paint and marker in 1990, answered artists moving away from traditional lettering. BLADE’s work stays recognizable for its ’70s-era palette, overlapping 3D letters and abstract imagery.
product_1_description: Edition of 3 hand-drawn USPS-style stickers, attached together to form a single piece. Each set features slight design variations, making every edition unique. Created by graffiti legend Blade. Measures 14.5" x 4.25" overall. Signed on the back.

subject: September T-Shirt Drop: ANNSI ARTE is Live
preheader: Bubble Softie won the vote. The styles that built graffiti, on one tee.
announcement_line_1: We Did It Again. Meet This Month’s Shirt Drop.
product_1_title: September AS COLOUR Drop: Annsi Arte
product_1_description: This month’s shirt highlights the evolution and diversity of graffiti styles throughout the years. Inspired by an important section of the Museum of Graffiti that showcases the many styles developed within the culture, the design celebrates the artists, lettering, and visual language that continue to shape graffiti. For the front of the tee, IG voted, and Bubble Softie was selected as the winning style, giving the shirt its bold centerpiece. The back features a collection of the other iconic styles, creating a visual timeline of graffiti’s ever-evolving aesthetic. This exclusive tee is locally hand-screen printed by graffiti artists in our community, keeping the production close to home and helping support the artists and creatives who make our culture what it is.

subject: Meet GIZ: From Subway Bombing to the Gallery Wall
preheader: Originals and hand-embellished prints from a New York writer since 1988.
bio_paragraph_1: GIZ, born in New York City in 1977, is celebrated for vibrant, transformative work that bridges the gritty urban landscapes of NYC with the polished echelons of the gallery scene.
bio_paragraph_2: He began at the age of 10 in 1988, rapidly becoming synonymous with the energetic and rebellious spirit of street art through an audacious campaign of bombing clean NYC subway trains.
bio_paragraph_3: In the early ’90s he initiated the ‘MTA’ (Most Talked About) street-bombing campaign, spreading his crew’s work across all five boroughs and laying the foundation for his evolution as an artist.

subject: Meet CASH4: Architectural Satire from Brooklyn
preheader: One-of-one originals from the writer who turned a scrap-car ad into a name.
bio_paragraph_1: CASH4 (Russell Murphy) is a Brooklyn-based contemporary artist and graffiti writer whose work bridges raw street culture with sharp architectural satire.
bio_paragraph_2: Born in Buffalo, New York in 1984, his gritty aesthetic was shaped by an industrial Rust Belt upbringing and formal training at Syracuse University, where he earned a Bachelor of Architecture.
bio_paragraph_3: That background in spatial design lets him reframe urban decay as a canvas — repurposing discarded political signs and cardboard into vibrant mixed-media paintings that critique consumerism and gentrification.
product_1_description: Original hand-painted artwork by CASH4, created directly on a 4.5 x 7 in. playing card. Medium: hand-painted poker playing card. Edition: 1 of 1.
